papers.title_in_file: Direct Generation and Detection of Correlated Photons with 3.2 um Wavelength Spacing
papers.version_note: arXiv:1708.05909v2, 13 Sep 2017; text matches the record.
papers.what_it_is: An experimental paper reporting SPDC pairs at 779.8 nm and 3950 nm in a PPLN waveguide, with the idler detected by upconversion to 651.2 nm and a Si-APD, and a coincidence-to-accidental ratio of 54.

assertions.value: The authors state that the SPDC process converts a 651.2 nm pump photon into a 779.8 nm signal photon and a 3950 nm idler photon.
quotes: For the current SPDC process where a 651.2 nm pump photon downconverts to a pair of a 779.8 nm signal photon and a 3950 nm idler photon.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 1 states the process wavelengths as the paper's own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the pair detuning is over 3.2 microns, or more than 300 THz, and claim it is the largest detuning thus far in any waveguide-based photon source.
quotes: The detuning of the pair is over 3.2 microns, or >300 THz, which is the largest detuning thus far in any waveguide-based photon source.
assertions.certainty_reason: A priority claim by the authors, with no survey in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that prior correlated-photon techniques have been developed only in the visible and near-IR spectra, and that photon pairs were generated at 3.1 microns only very recently, with similar wavelengths and rather limited correlation (attributed to other work).
quotes: but only in the visible and near-IR spectra
Only very recently, photon pairs have been generated at 3.1 microns, albeit with similar wavelengths and rather limited
assertions.certainty_reason: A literature statement attributed to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that the waveguide has a silicon-dioxide cladded core with 3.5 um height and 11 um top width ridge structure, designed so that all lightwaves are in their respective fundamental quasi-TM modes for maximum overlap, and that FEM simulation of the actual waveguide parameters indicates a good mode overlap.
quotes: a silicon-dioxide cladded core with 3.5 um height (D) and 11 um top width (Wt) ridge structure
so that all lightwaves are in their respective fundamental quasi-transverse-magnetic (quasi-TM) modes for the maximum overlap
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 1 states the device geometry as the paper's own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the waveguide is periodically poled with a domain length of 16.7 micron for quasi-phase matching, and that its temperature is stabilized at 32.2 ± 0.1 °C.
quotes: the waveguide is periodically poled with a domain length of 16.7 micron
stabilized at 32.2 ± 0.1 ◦C
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 1 states the poling and temperature as the paper's own setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that a 651.2 nm pulse train with 10 MHz repetition rate and 130 ps pulse width is coupled into a 2.2-cm long PPLN waveguide for SPDC.
quotes: A 651.2 nm pulse train with 10 MHz repetition rate and 130 ps pulse width is coupled
into a 2.2-cm long PPLN waveguide
assertions.certainty_reason: The Figure 2 caption states the pump and waveguide as setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that the signal photons pass a filter set of 3 nm bandwidth and are detected by a free-running fiber-coupled Si-APD (ID100) with 12.5 % quantum efficiency and dark-count rate below 1.4 Hz.
quotes: bandwidth: 3 nm; extinction: 140 dB
12.5 % quantum efﬁciency and low dark-count rate (<1.4 Hz)
assertions.certainty_reason: Figure 2 caption and Methods state the signal detector as setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that idler photons are upconverted by 779.8 nm pump pulses (779.8 nm + 3950 nm -> 651.2 nm) in a second PPLN waveguide with temperature stabilized at 62.2 ± 0.1 °C, and the 651.2 nm light is detected by a second Si-APD.
quotes: temperature stabilized at 62.2 ± 0.1 ◦C for the optimum phase matching
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the upconversion setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that the upconverted idler photons are detected by a free-running Si-APD (ID100) with 22.5% quantum efficiency and dark count below 1.8 Hz, behind an infrared narrow band filter with 60 nm FWHM in the Methods; the caption of the setup figure gives 90 nm for the same filter.
quotes: FWHM bandwidth: 60 nm
bandwidth: 90 nm; extinction: 70 dB
22.5% quantum efﬁciency and low dark count (< 1.8 Hz)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper gives two different filter bandwidths, so the setup value is not settled.
assertions.reader_inference: The Figure 2 caption (90 nm) and Methods (60 nm) disagree on the 3950 nm filter bandwidth; the Section 2 text also uses 22% for the same detector.

assertions.value: The authors report that the Si-APD has 50 ps timing resolution and the TDC has 66 ps root-mean-square timing resolution and 27 ps time-bin resolution.
quotes: The Si-APD has 50 ps timing resolution while the TDC has 66 ps root-mean-square timing resolution and 27 ps time-bin resolution.
assertions.certainty_reason: Methods states the timing hardware as setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that the signal-photon generation probability depends linearly on pump peak power, and that from the slope the SPDC efficiency is estimated to be -87 dB, about one in every 5 × 108 pump photons (exponent printed flat; read as ten to the eighth) downconverting into a correlated pair.
quotes: which displays a linear dependence, as expected
From the slope, the SPDC efﬁciency is estimated to be -87 dB
about one in every 5 × 108 pump photons
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement from a single device.

assertions.value: The authors report a single-photon pulse of 130 ps FWHM after the filters, an effective spectral bandwidth of 3 nm FWHM, and effectively 100 detected time-frequency modes at 780 nm.
quotes: shown a single-photon pulse of 130 ps full width at half maximum (FWHM) after the ﬁlters
The cascaded ﬁlters centered at 780 nm provide an effective spectral bandwidth of 3 nm (FWHM)
so that there are effectively 100 detected time-frequency modes
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement; the mode count is the authors' estimate.
assertions.reader_inference: Section 2 later uses 144 detected modes for the upconverted side; the 100 here is for the 780 nm side.

assertions.value: The paper states, citing other work, that superconducting nanowire detectors cover visible to mid-IR in principle but show a sharp decline in detection efficiency with a rapid rise of intrinsic dark count in the mid-IR regime.
quotes: there is a sharp decline in the detection efﬁciency accompanied by a rapid rise of intrinsic dark count in the mid-IR regime
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors report that the phase matching bandwidth of the upconversion waveguide is measured to be 5.6 nm FWHM, corresponding to 107 GHz.
quotes: The phase matching bandwidth of the waveguide is measured to be 5.6 nm (FWHM), corresponding to 107 GHz in spectral bandwidth.
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: Delta nu = c Delta lambda / lambda^2 at 3950 nm gives about 108 GHz, consistent with the stated 107 GHz.

assertions.value: The authors report a highest internal conversion efficiency of 33.9 ± 1.8% at an upconversion pump peak power of 3.8 W, with the efficiency decreasing as power rises further, which they attribute likely to multiple spatial modes.
quotes: with the highest conversion efﬁciency 33.9 ± 1.8% achieved at the peak pump power of 3.8 W
The efﬁciency decreases as the power further increases.
This saturation of conversion efﬁciency is likely due to the existence of multiple spatial modes for the photons.
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement on one device; the saturation cause is the authors' suggestion.
assertions.reader_inference: The efficiency is inferred from signal counts and independently characterized losses, not measured directly (Methods p.21).

assertions.value: The authors state that the internal conversion efficiency is derived by dividing the true upconverted idler counts (SPDC on minus SPDC off) by the correlated signal counts, after correcting for linear losses and Si-APD quantum efficiencies, with a measured loss of about 16 dB from SPDC output to upconversion waveguide output (about 3 dB mirror output coupling, 1 dB filters and dichroic, 12 dB input coupling and propagation).
quotes: the internal upconversion efﬁciency was characterized by dividing the true upconverted idler-photon counts by the correlated signal-photon counts
is measured to be about 16 dB by using a weak coherent light at 3950 nm
About 3 dB loss is caused by the output coupling loss of the off-axis parabolic mirror, 1 dB of loss is from the 3950 nm bandpass ﬁlters and dichroic beam splitters
another 12 dB is from the input coupling efﬁciency and propagation loss of the upconversion waveguide
assertions.certainty_reason: Methods defines how the internal efficiency is obtained.
assertions.reader_inference: Methods also gives 19 dB total transmission before the Si-APD and about 4 dB afterward; 16 + 4 = 20 dB differs from 19 dB, presumably rounding.

assertions.value: The authors report that modal decomposition of the joint spectral function finds about 15 SPDC modes, approximately BT/4, and that a coupled-equation simulation with no free fitting parameter agrees well with the measured conversion efficiency, with slight discrepancy attributed to neglected higher-order pump modes and propagation loss.
quotes: This calculation ﬁnds a total number of SPDC modes to be about 15, approximately equal to BT/4
which assumes no free ﬁtting parameter
It shows a good agreement with experimental results
assertions.certainty_reason: A single numerical simulation compared with one dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that with 33.9% conversion efficiency the noise photons are approximately 6.5×10−3 per pump pulse for 144 detected modes, and state this can be lowered to 4.5x10−5 per pulse if the number of detected modes is reduced to 1.
quotes: With a 33.9% conversion efﬁciency, the noise photons are approximately 6.5×10−3 per pump pulse for the 144 detected modes
4.5x10−5 per pulse if the number of the detected modes is reduced to 1
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement; the 1-mode value is a projection.
assertions.reader_inference: Methods p.22 gives 3.8×10−4 per pulse for 144 modes at optimum efficiency and the abstract gives 2.6×10−6 per mode; 6.5×10−3/144 is 4.5×10−5, so the Section 2 figure is about 17 times the Methods figure. The paper does not reconcile them.

assertions.value: The authors report a noise detection of about 3.8×10−4 per pulse with 144 detection modes at optimum conversion efficiency, including detector dark count, upconversion noise and blackbody radiation, and the abstract gives 2.6×10−6 photon noise per time-frequency mode.
quotes: about 3.8×10−4 per pulse with 144 detection modes
2.6×10−6 photon noise per time-frequency mode
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: 3.8×10−4/144 is 2.6×10−6, so the two statements agree with each other but not with Section 2's 6.5×10−3 per pulse.

assertions.value: The authors state that the majority of the noise counts come from spontaneous Raman scattering of the upconversion pump pulses falling in the filter window, that the noise count rate is higher with a wider bandpass filter, and that it depends linearly on pump peak power.
quotes: the majority of the dark counts are from the spontaneous Raman scattering of the upconversion pump pulses
the noise count rate is higher with wider bandpass ﬁlter
is linearly dependent on the pump peak power
assertions.certainty_reason: One measurement set with 144, 725 and 2900 modes.

assertions.value: The authors state that Raman scattering photons of the SPDC pump falling in the signal band are not expected to be significant because of the pump-signal detuning of more than 2500 cm−1.
quotes: is not expected to be signiﬁcant due to the large detuning between the pump and signal wavelength of more than 2500 cm−1
assertions.certainty_reason: An expectation stated without a measurement.

assertions.value: The authors state that the total detection efficiency of the 3950 nm photons is approximately 0.078% for the current under-optimized setup, and that it can be improved to 2.5% by shorter focal-length mirrors that cut waveguide coupling loss by 6 dB and Si-APDs with over 80% quantum efficiency.
quotes: the total detection efﬁciency of the 3950 nm single photons is approximately 0.078% for the current under-optimized setup
It can be improved signiﬁcantly to 2.5%
with over 80% quantum efﬁciency
reduce the total waveguide coupling loss by 6 dB
assertions.certainty_reason: The 0.078% is a derived figure for one setup; the 2.5% is a projection.

assertions.value: The authors define a coincident detection as both Si-APDs clicking within the coincidence window and an accidental coincidence as both clicking outside it, and obtain true coincidences by subtracting accidental from total coincidences.
quotes: A coincident detection is registered when both Si-APD
an accidentalcoincidence detection is recorded when both Si-APDs click outside the coincidence window

depends quadratically on the pump peak power

limited by the uncorrelated noise photons and dark counts of the upconversion detection system
we obtained a true coincidence count of 275 within an integration time of 300 s

quotes: For lower pump power, the CAR is only around 10∼20
the multiphoton effect involving the simultaneous generation of more than a photon pair increases the probability of accidental-coincidence detection

assertions.value: The authors report, from total detection efficiencies of 1.3% (signal) and 0.078% (idler), a photon pair production rate of about 9.4 × 104 pair per second (exponent printed flat; read as ten to the fourth) and a spectral brightness of 4.4 × 102 pair/s/nm/mW (ten squared), and expect two orders of magnitude improvement with GHz-repetition-rate pump pulses.
quotes: Considering the total detection efﬁciency of 1.3% and 0.078% for the signal and idler
the photon pair production rate is about 9.4 × 104 pair per second
spectral brightness of 4.4 × 102 pair/s/nm/mW

assertions.value: The authors state that a CAR of 54 gives a Franson visibility of 96% for time-energy entanglement, on par with existing SPDC sources in common wavelengths,.

quotes: the generation of idlers photons at 3950 nm can be heralded, with a second-order correlation g2(0) = 0.08 ± 0.015

papers.title_in_file: Photonic Nonlinearities via Quantum Zeno Blockade
papers.version_note: arXiv:1303.5666v1 (22 Mar 2013), Letter plus supplementary material (pages 6 and 7 of the text layer).
papers.what_it_is: A theory and simulation Letter proposing a deterministic single-photon phase gate from quantum Zeno blockade in a lithium-niobate microdisk resonator with sum-frequency generation.

assertions.value: The authors report that, for a lithium-niobate microresonator, a deterministic phase gate can be realized between single photons with near-unity fidelity.
quotes: we ﬁnd that a deterministic phase gate can be realized between single photons with near-unity ﬁdelity
assertions.certainty_reason: A simulation result with parameters the authors chose; no experiment.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is a numerical simulation, not a device measurement.

assertions.value: The authors state that, once the multimode nature of light propagation in a Kerr medium is taken into account, no useful cross-phase modulation effect can be produced in such systems even with an unrealistically giant Kerr nonlinearity (cited to refs 16 and 17).
quotes: it was recently discovered that no useful XPM eﬀect can be produced in such systems even with an unrealistically giant Kerr nonlinearity [16, 17]
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work (Shapiro 2006; Gea-Banacloche 2010).

assertions.value: The authors state that the fundamental reason is that causality prohibits a non-negligible cross-phase modulation phase shift without significant quantum noise.
quotes: The fundamental reason turns out to be that causality prohibits XPM phase shift of any non-negligible amount without signiﬁcant quantum noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: Attributed to earlier work in the same paragraph; not derived here.

assertions.value: The authors state that the intuition that a weak Kerr nonlinearity can give a single-photon cross-phase shift, if the nonlinearity is giant enough, rests on an incorrect single-mode argument.
quotes: This logic, unfortunately, is based on an incorrect single-mode argument.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated by the authors, supported by citation to refs 16 and 17.

assertions.value: The authors describe quantum Zeno blockade as occurring when a quantum system interacts with external degrees of freedom through a nonlinear channel, so that with strong nonlinear coupling a single photon in a mode can block (suppress) additional photons from coupling into that mode.
quotes: which occurs when a quantum system interacts with external degrees of freedom through a nonlinear channel
occupation of a certain quantum mode by a single photon can “block” (more precisely, suppress) additional photons from coupling into that mode [18, 19]
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own working definition of quantum Zeno blockade, Introduction p.1.

assertions.value: The authors set up the gate as a lithium-niobate microdisk cavity evanescently coupled to a prism, with the cavity designed to be in resonance with both the pump (control) and the signal (target).
quotes: It consists of a LN microdisk cavity evanescently coupled to a prism.
The cavity is designed to be in resonance with both the pump (control) and the signal (target).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own gate setup, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that the chi-2 nonlinearity of lithium niobate can lead to intracavity sum-frequency or difference-frequency generation between signal and pump, and that only sum-frequency generation is considered as a specific example.
quotes: The χ(2) nonlinearity of LN can lead to intracavity sum-frequency generation (SFG) or diﬀerencefrequency generation (DFG) between the signal and the pump.
Only SFG is considered in the following as a speciﬁc example.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper limits its analysis to sum-frequency generation, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that with the pump off the signal field couples into the disk through the prism and then exits with a pi phase shift relative to its input.
quotes: Through the prism, the signal ﬁeld evanescently couples into the disk and then exits with a π phase shift relative to its input.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's description of the pump-off gate operation, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in either the CQZ or the IQZ regime, with the pump on the signal's coupling into the disk is suppressed and the signal reflects (exits) with its phase unchanged.
quotes: In either the CQZ or the IQZ regime, the signal’s coupling into disk is thus suppressed and it reﬂects (exits) with its phase unchanged.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's description of the pump-on gate operation, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors define the coherent quantum Zeno (CQZ) regime as the case where the cavity is resonant for the sum-frequency field with high intrinsic quality factor; coherent sum-frequency generation then acts as a continuous measurement that shifts the disk away from resonance with the signal, preventing the signal photon from entering the cavity.
quotes: In the CQZ case, the cavity is resonant for the SF ﬁeld with high intrinsic quality factor
Coherent SFG process thus works as a continuous measurement, which shifts the disk away from resonance with the signal, preventing the signal photon from entering the cavity.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of the CQZ regime, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors define the incoherent quantum Zeno (IQZ) regime as the case with a short-lived cavity sum-frequency field, which together with the high potential for sum-frequency generation opens a strong dissipation channel for the intracavity signal field, destroying the cavity resonance and preventing the signal photon from entering.
quotes: In the IQZ case, a short-lived cavity SF ﬁeld, together with the high potential for SFG, opens a strong dissipation channel for the intracavity signal ﬁeld,
destroying the cavity resonance and preventing the signal photon from entering the cavity.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of the IQZ regime, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that for a typical lithium-niobate microdisk with radius about 1.5 mm (as printed in the text layer) and intrinsic Q above the printed value 107, the resonance linewidth is much smaller than the free-spectral range, so only a single cavity mode is excited by each applied quasi-monochromatic field.
quotes: For a typical LN microdisk with radius R ≃ 1.5 mm and Qi > 107 [27], the resonance linewidth is much smaller than the cavity’s free-spectral range.
It is thus valid to consider only a single cavity mode being excited by the corresponding applied external quasimonochromatic ﬁeld.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' stated modeling scope, p.2.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer prints the radius as 1.5 mm, while the later disks are tens of micrometres; the unit may be a text-layer or typesetting error, which this reader cannot settle from the text.

quotes: To capture the temporal behavior of pulsed optical signals, a temporally multimode quantum description is needed.

quotes: vg is the group velocity which is assumed to be the same for all the pulsed ﬁelds

papers.title_in_file: Answer Partitions and Oracle Access Determine Quantum Query Complexity
papers.what_it_is: A short theory paper on quantum query complexity that formulates exact one-query answer-partition resolution as block discrimination of a unitary oracle family, proves a response-spectrum theorem for Deutsch's problem, and reports a census of balanced three-bit and four-bit partitions.

assertions.value: The paper defines the answer partition induced by a task g from the finite instance set to the set of answers as the set of cells formed by the preimages of the answers, and calls it the kinematic partition.
quotes: Let Ω be a finite instance set and let g : Ω → J specify the required answer. The task induces the answer partition (also called here the kinematic partition)
Πg = {Cj : j ∈ g(Ω)}, Cj = g−1(j).
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition stated in the paper's setup, Eq. (1).

assertions.value: The authors state that the answer partition is bookkeeping and is not by itself an access model or a complexity statement; in the query model the hidden instance labels a black-box transformation, and the operational question is whether a specified oracle and fixed protocol can transfer the cell label to an accessible output.
quotes: This partition is indispensable bookkeeping, but it is not yet an access model or a complexity statement.
The operational question is whether the specified oracle and a fixed protocol can transfer the cell label to an accessible output.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own framing and scope on p.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that an oracle problem pairs an answer partition with an access model for the hidden instance, and that quantum query speedup therefore belongs to the task-oracle pair.
quotes: An oracle problem pairs an answer partition with an access model for the hidden instance.
Quantum query speedup therefore belongs to the task–oracle pair.
assertions.certainty_reason: The thesis is the author's framing, which the examples in the paper illustrate; it is not itself a theorem.

assertions.value: The paper defines exact resolution after T queries as the existence of one instance-independent projective measurement, with projectors summing to the identity, under which the outcome for the cell of instance a occurs with probability one; supports of different cells are orthogonal and no orthogonality is required within a cell.
quotes: Exact resolution means that there is one instance-independent measurement {Pj} satisfying
Consequently, supports belonging to different cells are orthogonal; no orthogonality is required within a cell.
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition stated in the paper, Eq. (2).

assertions.value: The authors state that the cells are sets of classical instances, not subspaces, that the answer sectors arise only after an oracle and protocol have encoded them, and that the partition specifies a required zero pattern in the output distinguishability matrix rather than a ready-made physical observable.
quotes: The Cj themselves remain sets of classical instances. They are not subspaces, and the answer sectors PjHout arise only after an oracle and protocol have encoded them.
The partition therefore specifies a required zero pattern in the output distinguishability matrix rather than a readymade physical observable.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of what the partition is and is not, on p.1.

assertions.value: Proposition 1 (block discrimination): the partition is exactly resolvable with at most one use of the unitary oracle family {Ua}, allowing an arbitrary reference, if and only if there is a density operator sigma such that Tr(sigma Ua-dagger Ua') = 0 whenever g(a) differs from g(a'). The authors argue that exact discrimination requires the spans of output states of different cells to be orthogonal, and that orthogonal cell spans can be measured by their support projectors.
quotes: Proposition 1 (block discrimination). The partition Πg is exactly resolvable with at most one use of {Ua}, allowing an arbitrary reference, if and only if there is a density operator σ such that
Tr σUa†Ua′ = 0 whenever g(a) ≠ g(a′). (5)
Indeed, exact discrimination requires the spans of the output states associated with different cells to be orthogonal, which is equivalent to the indicated pairwise inner products vanishing.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as Proposition 1 with its conditions, followed by a short proof argument in the text.
assertions.reader_inference: The proof is a few lines and rests on standard perfect unitary discrimination arguments, as the paper itself says.

assertions.value: The authors state that the block-discrimination criterion is the direct form of standard perfect unitary-discrimination conditions (citing Acin, and Duan, Feng and Ying) and is not a new general channel-discrimination theorem; its role is to connect an answer partition to a specified oracle family.
quotes: is the direct block-discrimination form of standard perfect unitarydiscrimination conditions [2, 3]; it is not a new general channel-discrimination theorem.
Its role here is to connect an answer partition to a specified oracle family.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result attributed to prior work, with the paper's own framing of novelty.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Gram matrix need only be block diagonal according to the partition, that states within one cell may overlap or coincide, and that complete identification is the singleton-cell special case, where the Gram matrix must be diagonal.
quotes: The Gram matrix need only be block diagonal according to Πg; states within one cell may overlap or coincide.
Complete identification is the singleton-cell special case, where G must be diagonal.
assertions.certainty_reason: Direct consequence of Proposition 1, stated in the text on p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that for bounded error orthogonality is replaced by a common POVM with the required success probability, and that multiquery state conversion and function evaluation are characterized by adversary methods (citing Lee et al. and Reichardt).
quotes: For bounded error, orthogonality is replaced by a common POVM with the required success probability.
Multiquery state conversion and function evaluation are characterized by adversary methods [4, 5].
assertions.certainty_reason: Attributed to cited work [4, 5]; not proved here.

assertions.value: The authors state that Eq. (5) characterizes exact resolvability with at most one oracle use; for every nontrivial partition zero queries cannot resolve the task, so this is equivalent to exact quantum complexity of one, while the trivial one-cell partition has complexity zero. They state that the criterion does not by itself establish an advantage, which additionally requires a gap between quantum and classical complexity for the same task and oracle interface.
quotes: Equation (5) characterizes exact resolvability with at most one oracle use, namely QE(Πg; U ) ≤ 1.
For every nontrivial partition, zero queries cannot resolve the task, so this is equivalent to QE(Πg; U ) = 1; the trivial one-cell partition instead has QE(Πg; U ) = 0.
Speedup additionally requires a gap between Qϵ and Rϵ for the same task and oracle interface.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated with conditions in the text on p.2 as a consequence of Proposition 1.

assertions.value: The authors state that a deterministic classical query protocol partitions the instance set by its possible transcripts and succeeds exactly only when that transcript partition refines the answer partition, whereas a quantum protocol need not create an intermediate classical transcript and changes overlaps among hypothesis states, measuring only after the cells have separated.
quotes: Classically, a deterministic query protocol partitions Ω by its possible transcripts and succeeds exactly only when that transcript partition refines Πg.
A quantum protocol need not create such an intermediate classical transcript; it changes the overlaps among the hypothesis states and measures only after the required cells have separated.
assertions.certainty_reason: A conceptual statement in the text without a separate formal proof.

assertions.value: The authors state that if two oracle families are related by instance-independent unitaries on both sides, the attainable Gram matrices are unchanged as the probe varies; families that exactly simulate one another with a constant number of oracle calls have quantum query complexities equal up to constant factors. They state that exact one-query behavior can nevertheless change when the response representation is not of this form.
quotes: for instance-independent unitaries A, B, then Va†Va′ = B†Ua†Ua′ B; as the probe varies, the attainable Gram matrices are unchanged.
families that exactly simulate one another with O(1) oracle calls have quantum query complexities equal up to constant factors
Exact onequery behavior can nevertheless change when the response representation is not of the form Eq. (6).
assertions.certainty_reason: Gram-matrix invariance follows directly from the displayed identity in the text on p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that Hadamard conjugation of the answer qubit turns the standard XOR oracle into the full controlled-phase action, so the two forms are exactly equivalent, whereas the restricted sign oracle is only a subroutine because complementary truth tables differ by a global phase. They state that supplying a coherent control for it restores the missing relative phase but is additional black-box access rather than an automatic operation on an unknown unitary (citing Araujo et al.).
quotes: Hadamard conjugation of the answer qubit turns Eq. (7) below into the full controlled-phase action |x, z⟩ → (−1)zbx |x, z⟩, so the two forms are exactly equivalent.
complementary truth tables differ by a global phase.
coherent control is additional blackbox access rather than an automatic operation on an unknown unitary [6].
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the text; the control-access point is attributed to cited work [6].

assertions.value: The paper shows with explicit output states that for Deutsch's problem with the answer qubit in the minus state, phase kickback gives output states on the address register such that the constant and balanced cells occupy orthogonal rays while the two instances inside either cell are not distinguished. The authors state that this is a block-diagonal, but not diagonal, Gram matrix and gives the familiar one versus two exact-query separation.
quotes: Thus the constant and balanced cells occupy orthogonal rays, while the two instances inside either cell are not distinguished.
This is precisely a block-diagonal, but not diagonal, Gram matrix and gives the familiar one versus two exact-query separation [7].
assertions.certainty_reason: Explicit output states of Eq. (8) are given in the paper and the cell orthogonality follows by inspection.

assertions.value: Theorem 1 (response spectrum): the Deutsch constant-balanced partition is exactly one-query resolvable through the controlled-response family {Ub(V)}, with arbitrary probes and references, if and only if -1 is an eigenvalue of the response unitary V. The family is defined for any unitary V by the controlled application of V to the power of the truth-table bit at each address.

Theorem 1 (response spectrum). The Deutsch
constant–balanced partition is exactly one-query resolvable through {Ub(V )}, with arbitrary probes and references, if and only if −1 is an eigenvalue of V .

Since the modulus of each z_x is bounded by p_x, the equations force p0 = p1 = 1/2 and z0 = z1 = -1/2, and equality in the unitary expectation bound is possible only when the support of each nonzero response operator lies in the -1 eigenspace of V.

Equality in the unitary expectation bound is possible only when the support of each nonzero ρx lies in the −1 eigenspace of V .
px = Tr ρx, zx = Tr(ρxV ), p0 + p1 = 1. (10)

They state that the theorem holds the four Deutsch instances fixed and varies the response unitary, which differs from qudit versions of Deutsch-Jozsa that use higher-dimensional address and response systems (citing Cereceda), and from prior-distribution useless-query bounds (citing Meyer and Pommersheim).
quotes: Conversely, a −1 eigenvector provides ordinary phase kickback and Eq. (8).
The theorem above instead holds the four Deutsch instances fixed and varies the response unitary.

assertions.value: Corollary 1 (cyclic response): for the elementary cyclic response X_d mapping y to y+1 modulo d, with d at least 2, computational-basis queries return the same Boolean point value for every d, but -1 occurs in the spectrum of X_d exactly when d is even. The paper gives exact quantum query complexity of one for even d and two for odd d, and classical deterministic complexity of two.

but −1 occurs in the spectrum of Xd exactly when d is even.

Hence one query is possible only for N at most 2, with Deutsch as the limiting case.

Exact even–odd separation would require pi = 1/2 for every i, while normalization gives i pi ≤ 1. Hence one query is possible only for N ≤ 2, with Deutsch as the limiting case.

The lower bound uses that the acceptance probability of a T-query algorithm is a polynomial of degree at most 2T in the input bits whereas parity has exact degree N, and applying the Deutsch construction to disjoint pairs gives the matching algorithm (citing Beals et al. and Farhi et al.).

QE(ParN ) = ⌈N/2⌉, D(ParN ) = N (15)
for point-value access [10, 11].

assertions.value: The authors state that if one declares an oracle that XORs the parity of the whole input into the answer register to be a single call, parity becomes one-query resolvable classically as well as quantum mechanically; this does not defeat the exact parity result, since it replaces point access by an oracle that already aggregates the desired answer.

it replaces point access by an oracle that already aggregates the desired answer.

assertions.value: The paper sets up a census in which the hidden instance is an N-bit string accessed through the Boolean point oracle with the address range enlarged to N, over every binary answer map with equal-sized cells; the number of such unlabeled partitions is given by a closed formula. Coordinate permutations, independent complements and answer exchange preserve point-oracle query cost and reduce the 35 three-bit partitions to six orbits and the 6435 four-bit partitions to 58.
quotes: consider every binary answer map having 2N−1 instances in each cell.

Coordinate permutations, independent complements of coordinates, and answer exchange preserve the pointoracle query cost. They reduce the M3 = 35 partitions to six orbits and the M4 = 6435 partitions to 58.

assertions.value: The authors report that for each partition they computed the optimal classical deterministic decision-tree depth D and sought matching bounds on exact quantum query complexity; one-query feasibility was solved over the rationals, multiquery feasibility used the Gram-matrix semidefinite program of Barnum, Saks and Szegedy, and constructive upper bounds were adaptive trees whose nodes read one bit or the parity of two bits. The authors state that such trees are certificates but not a general characterization of exact quantum algorithms.
quotes: For each partition we computed the optimal classic deterministic decision-tree depth D and sought matching bounds on the exact quantum query complexity QE.
Multiquery feasibility was formulated with the Gram-matrix semidefinite program of Barnum, Saks, and Szegedy [12].
Such trees are useful certificates, but they are not a general characterization of exact quantum algorithms [13].

assertions.value: The authors report cross-validating their orbit representatives against the published NPN identifiers of Montanaro, Jozsa and Mitchison: after removing dummy variables, the one- and two-query entries agree with all 15 representatives certified here, and for the remaining 43 representatives the reported optimal two-query success probabilities lie between 0.900 and 0.986, consistent with the infeasibility results but still numerical. They state this checks the enumeration and symmetry bookkeeping and does not give an exact lower bound.

For the 43 remaining representatives, its reported optimal two-query success probabilities lie between 0.900 and 0.986, consistent with our infeasibility results but still numerical.

assertions.certainty_reason: A comparison with a prior numerical study; the numbers are the paper's report.
assertions.reader_inference: The 15 certified plus 43 numerical representatives total 58, matching the orbit count.

The authors state that basis queries still return a . x exactly, and that the witness removes coherences between sectors with different x_S.

The authors state this is an access-induced change of the task-oracle pair, not a same-partition comparison for the original singleton task.

assertions.value: The paper shows that after Bernstein-Vazirani phase kickback and tracing out the witness the state is a sum over address pairs agreeing on S, and that after the final Hadamards character orthogonality gives the projector on the coordinates of a outside S tensor the maximally mixed state on S, with outcome probability 2^-k times an indicator that the outside-S coordinates of the outcome equal those of a. The authors conclude the one-query readout exactly resolves the surviving partition and that zero queries cannot, because the output would be independent of its cell label.
quotes: Character orthogonality after the final Hadamards gives, up to a fixed reordering of coordinates,
Pr(z|a) = 2−k 1[zS¯ = aS¯].
Thus the one-query readout exactly resolves ΠS. Zero queries cannot resolve this nontrivial partition ΠS, because the output would be independent of its cell label.
assertions.certainty_reason: Derivation given by the paper in Eqs. (21)-(22).

assertions.value: The authors argue that the classical upper bound uses the basis queries outside S. For the lower bound they impose the promise that a is zero on S; under the uniform distribution on the remaining coordinates, fewer than n - k returned linear equations leave an affine solution space of positive dimension, so even a decoder given the complete transcript succeeds with probability at most 1/2, and the same average bound holds with internal randomness, so some input has success at most 1/2.

The same average bound holds after including the protocol’s internal randomness, and therefore some input has success at most 1/2.
assertions.certainty_reason: Averaging argument with its promise condition stated in the text on p.4.

assertions.value: The authors state that if the witness were coherently available, the fixed coupling could be undone without another oracle call, restoring the ordinary Bernstein-Vazirani output, and that the accessible oracle here is a channel rather than the globally unitary dilation, which highlights the distinction between standard and garbage-bearing oracle access (citing Aaronson).

The accessible oracle here is a channel rather than the globally unitary dilation

assertions.value: The authors state that the witness model separates loss of the phase-interference route from loss of the classical function values themselves.
quotes: The model separates loss of the phase-interference route from loss of the classical function values themselves.
assertions.certainty_reason: An interpretive statement about the model by the author.

assertions.value: The authors state that the useful resource is the structure of the oracle response (its phases, spectrum, accessible registers and possible environment) rather than the formal number of branches in a superposition, and that rewriting an oracle by fixed basis changes preserves discrimination whereas changing its response representation, aggregating information, or discarding a witness can alter it.
quotes: The useful resource is consequently the structure of the oracle response—its phases, spectrum, accessible registers, and possible environment— rather than simply the formal number of branches in a superposition.
Rewriting an oracle by fixed basis changes preserves this discrimination, whereas changing its response representation, aggregating information, or discarding a witness can alter it [1].
assertions.certainty_reason: An interpretive claim in the introduction, partly attributed to [1] and illustrated by the later examples.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that partitions are indispensable as specifications but insufficient as complexity criteria, that quantum advantage is not caused by partition coarseness or simultaneous access to imagined branch values, and that it occurs when structure-matched interference separates the required answer cells in fewer calls than any classical transcript under the same interface.
quotes: Partitions are therefore indispensable as specifications but insufficient as complexity criteria.
Quantum advantage is not caused by partition coarseness or by simultaneous access to imagined branch values.
It occurs when structure-matched interference separates the required answer cells in fewer calls than any classical transcript under the same interface.
assertions.certainty_reason: The author's concluding interpretation of the results.

assertions.value: The authors state that superlinear exact separations for total Boolean functions are known (citing Ambainis), but that establishing any asymptotic speedup requires a structured family of task-oracle pairs and that percentages from a finite census cannot substitute for that analysis.
quotes: Superlinear exact separations for total Boolean functions are known [18], but establishing any asymptotic speedup requires a structured family of task–oracle pairs; percentages from a finite census cannot substitute for that analysis.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the limit of its own census results on p.5.

assertions.value: The authors state that Shor's and Grover's algorithms fit the task-oracle perspective: Shor exploits periodic structure in the oracle family accessible via the quantum Fourier transform, and Grover exploits symmetry and coherent amplitude amplification via a matched phase oracle. They state that quantum speedup depends on the structure of the oracle access rather than on the coarseness or cardinality of the answer partition alone.
quotes: Shor exploits periodic structure in the oracle family accessible via the quantum Fourier transform, while Grover exploits symmetry and coherent amplitude amplification via a matched phase oracle.
quantum speedup depends on the structure of the oracle access, rather than on the coarseness or cardinality of the answer partition alone.
assertions.certainty_reason: A discussion remark without a derivation in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that the exact three-bit certificates show how quantum advantages can arise from oracle-accessible, conditionally composed refinements, while the four-bit calculation separates exact certificates from numerical candidates.
